claims.text: The initial material is a Ta-based refractory alloy with a disordered BCC solid-solution structure.
Ta-containing multicomponent refractory alloys can exhibit phase separation or segregation.
Ta-based refractory alloys exhibit complex liquid structure.
Full DFT thermodynamic integration over the relevant phase space is prohibitively expensive for multicomponent alloys.
Standard EAM potentials poorly describe the liquid structure of multicomponent refractory alloys.
Liquid short-range order and local coordination are highly sensitive to the multicomponent character of the alloy.
EAM potentials fail in refractory liquids because their pairwise or simple many-body forms cannot represent composition-dependent electronic screening and local ordering.
An MLP trained exclusively on high-temperature AIMD liquid configurations can capture liquid short-range order and coordination environments.
Learning the liquid potential-energy surface accurately enables accurate calculation of liquid entropy and enthalpy.
An MLP-based perturbation or simplified integration path can replace full DFT thermodynamic integration for the solid-liquid free-energy difference.
The MLP-based scheme will produce melting free-energy differences or melting points within 5% of DFT benchmarks.
An EAM-based method will have greater than 20% error in the predicted melting point.
The predicted EAM melting-point error is caused by incorrect modeling of multicomponent liquid short-range order.
The MLP perturbation scheme will reduce computational cost by a factor of 10 to 100 relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.
At least 200 atoms are required to capture the relevant multicomponent correlations.
Insufficient high-temperature or composition-specific liquid training data can cause the MLP to fail to generalize and yield inaccurate free energies.
A poorly defined solid-liquid perturbation path can introduce free-energy errors.
Complex phase transitions not represented by the MLP can invalidate the perturbation calculation.

contradictions.description: The MLP is specified as being trained exclusively on liquid configurations, yet it is then used to determine a solid-liquid free-energy difference and described as perturbing from a solid reference. No solid training, validation, or separate solid reference potential is specified, so the proposed use extends beyond the stated training domain.
